title: Subscribe
subtitle: 本課限定語境：subscribe = to arrange to receive a publication, service, channel, newsletter, or m
description: 本課限定語境：subscribe = to arrange to receive a publication, service, channel, newsletter, or membership regularly, often by registering and sometimes by paying · 「訂閱；登記接收；加入訂閱服務」

words.note: 表示登記加入服務、電子郵件名單、網站、活動或計劃。
words.example: You can sign up for the newsletter on our website.
words.exampleZh: 你可以在我們的網站登記訂閱電子報。

exercises.original: You can subscribe to our weekly newsletter on the website.
exercises.zh: 你可以在網站登記訂閱我們的每週電子報。
exercises.upgrade: You can sign up for our weekly newsletter on the website.

options.explanation: newsletter + on the website 是典型線上登記語境；sign up for a newsletter 是非常自然的搭配。
renew 表示延長既有訂閱，原句沒有「已經訂過」的資訊。
是商標註冊，語義完全不同。
一次性購買不能表達持續收到 newsletter。
意思相反。
enrol 適合課程，且這個結構不適合 newsletter。

exercises.original: Thousands of users subscribed to receive product updates by email.
exercises.zh: 數千名用戶登記以電郵接收產品更新。
exercises.upgrade: Thousands of users signed up to receive product updates by email.

options.explanation: to receive product updates by email 表示加入更新名單，sign up 很自然，而且不暗示付款。
renew contract 是延續既有合約，原句只是加入更新服務。
購買產品和接收更新不是同一行為。
語境不符。
是公司登記，不是使用者訂閱。
方向相反。

exercises.original: Visitors can subscribe for free to receive event announcements.
exercises.zh: 訪客可以免費登記接收活動公告。
exercises.upgrade: Visitors can sign up for free to receive event announcements.

options.explanation: for free + receive event announcements 表明是免費加入通知名單。
paid 和原句 for free 直接矛盾。
沒有既有訂閱。
購票和接收公告不同。
是退出訂閱。
不是此類登記。

words.note: 表示正式建立一段期間的訂閱關係，通常涉及定期付款。
words.example: She took out a subscription to the digital magazine.
words.exampleZh: 她訂閱了這本數碼雜誌。

exercises.original: She subscribed to the digital magazine for one year.
exercises.zh: 她辦理了一年的數碼雜誌訂閱。
exercises.upgrade: She took out a subscription to the digital magazine for one year.

options.explanation: registering on a site may be required, but it does not necessarily mean she paid for a one-year magazine subscription.
for one year + digital magazine is a formal, time-limited subscription arrangement, exactly matching this phrase.
following a magazine account is not the same as purchasing access to the publication.
renewal implies an existing subscription period ending and continuing; the sentence only states the subscription itself.
course enrollment is unrelated.
means she chose not to participate.

exercises.original: He subscribed to a premium streaming service for twelve months.
exercises.zh: 他辦理了十二個月的進階串流服務訂閱。
exercises.upgrade: He took out a subscription to a premium streaming service for twelve months.

options.explanation: premium + for twelve months strongly suggests a formal paid subscription.

options.text: signed up for a free trial of
options.explanation: a trial is temporary and free; the sentence specifies a twelve-month subscription.
not the standard relation to a streaming service.
one-off purchase differs from ongoing subscription access.
account creation alone does not guarantee a paid plan.
opposite direction.

exercises.original: The library subscribed to several academic journals for its staff.
exercises.zh: 圖書館為員工辦理了數種學術期刊訂閱。
exercises.upgrade: The library took out subscriptions to several academic journals for its staff.

options.explanation: several academic journals in an institutional access context strongly points to formal subscriptions.
usernames may be part of access administration, but not the subscription itself.
following people does not provide journal access.
single-issue purchases are one-off, unlike continuing journal subscriptions.
wrong activity type.
means declined participation.

words.note: 表示提供個人資料以建立帳戶、取得服務或完成正式登記。
words.example: Users must register before they can access the premium content.
words.exampleZh: 用戶必須先註冊，才可存取進階內容。

exercises.original: Users must subscribe on the website before they can create a profile.
exercises.zh: 用戶必須先在網站註冊，才可以建立個人資料。
exercises.upgrade: Users must register on the website before they can create a profile.

options.explanation: on the website + create a profile indicates account registration rather than paid subscription.
requires a pre-existing account or subscription nearing expiry.
the service is a website profile, not a publication subscription.
means refuse or leave a service.
opposite action.
course/programme language does not fit profile creation.

exercises.original: To subscribe to the platform, you first need to enter your name and email address.
exercises.zh: 要加入平台，你首先需要輸入姓名和電郵地址完成註冊。
exercises.upgrade: To register for the platform, you first need to enter your name and email address.

options.explanation: providing name and email is a classic registration step; the sentence does not yet mention payment or ongoing content.
requires something already active.
wrong object and transaction type.
opposite consent direction.
opposite action.
education-specific and unrelated.

exercises.original: New members can subscribe online and receive an account immediately.
exercises.zh: 新會員可以網上註冊並立即取得帳戶。
exercises.upgrade: New members can register online and receive an account immediately.

options.explanation: receive an account immediately makes account creation the key clue, so register is the best fit.
renewal continues an existing arrangement; these are new members.
does not normally create an account.
not account registration.
means leave a mailing/service list.
wrong activity.

words.meaning: 報名；登記加入課程／計劃
words.note: 表示正式加入課程、培訓、教育計劃或某些會員制度。
words.example: She enrolled in the online course last week.
words.exampleZh: 她上星期報讀了網上課程。

exercises.original: Students can subscribe to the online training programme from next Monday.
exercises.zh: 學生可以由下星期一起報讀網上培訓計劃。
exercises.upgrade: Students can enrol in the online training programme from next Monday.

options.explanation: students + training programme is classic enrollment language.
only applies if students are already enrolled and extending participation.
may mean follow content informally, but not formally join a programme.

options.text: take out a magazine subscription to
options.explanation: subscription phrase fits publications/services, not a training programme.
opposite direction.
unrelated legal registration.

exercises.original: She subscribed to a professional development course offered by her employer.
exercises.zh: 她報讀了僱主提供的專業發展課程。
exercises.upgrade: She enrolled in a professional development course offered by her employer.

options.explanation: professional development course requires formal course participation, making enrol the natural verb.
following course content is not the same as officially joining the course.
no prior course registration is mentioned.
wrong object.
opposite.
means declined to participate.

exercises.original: Employees may subscribe to the leadership programme after six months with the company.
exercises.zh: 員工入職六個月後可報名參加領導力計劃。
exercises.upgrade: Employees may enrol in the leadership programme after six months with the company.

options.explanation: leadership programme + eligibility after six months clearly describes formal programme enrollment.
would require existing participation.
a programme place may involve fees, but buy does not express becoming a participant.
too informal and does not imply formal registration.
opposite direction.
unrelated digital registration.

words.note: 表示成為一個群組、服務、會員計劃或社群的一員。
words.example: He joined the premium membership programme.
words.exampleZh: 他加入了進階會員計劃。

exercises.original: Customers can subscribe to the loyalty programme at any store.
exercises.zh: 顧客可以在任何分店加入忠誠會員計劃。
exercises.upgrade: Customers can join the loyalty programme at any store.

options.explanation: loyalty programme is a membership scheme, so join is a natural, broad alternative.
only if membership is expiring.
does not create membership status.
making a purchase is not the same as joining the programme.
means decline participation.
means end membership.

exercises.original: She subscribed to the local book club last month.
exercises.zh: 她上個月加入了本地讀書會。
exercises.upgrade: She joined the local book club last month.

options.explanation: book club is a group/community, and join is the standard verb for becoming a member.
would mean continuing existing membership.
following the club online does not imply membership.
wrong sense of register.
purchase does not equal club membership.
opposite.

exercises.original: More than 10,000 people have subscribed to the membership programme.
exercises.zh: 超過一萬人已加入這個會員計劃。
exercises.upgrade: More than 10,000 people have joined the membership programme.

options.explanation: membership programme makes membership status the core meaning, so join is concise and natural.
renew normally takes subscription/membership, not the newspaper itself, and the object is wrong.
following content is not membership.
one purchase does not imply joining.
opposite.
also opposite.

words.meaning: 主動選擇加入；同意接收
words.note: 表示主動同意接收通知、行銷電郵、資料分享或某項服務。
words.example: Customers can opt in to receive promotional emails.
words.exampleZh: 顧客可以主動選擇接收宣傳電郵。

exercises.original: Customers can subscribe to receive marketing emails if they wish.
exercises.zh: 顧客如願意，可以主動選擇接收市場推廣電郵。
exercises.upgrade: Customers can opt in to receive marketing emails if they wish.

options.explanation: if they wish signals voluntary consent, and marketing emails are a classic opt-in context.
there is no existing subscription period being extended.
wrong object and activity type.
marketing emails are not being purchased.
opposite action.
not a meaningful subscription alternative.

exercises.original: Users may subscribe to notifications about security updates.
exercises.zh: 用戶可以主動選擇接收保安更新通知。
exercises.upgrade: Users may opt in to notifications about security updates.

options.explanation: notifications are optional communications, so explicit consent is the key idea.
notifications do not normally have a fixed subscription term that needs renewal.
programme/course language does not fit notifications.
no payment is involved.
means stop receiving notifications.
unrelated.

exercises.original: New users are asked whether they want to subscribe to personalized recommendations.
exercises.zh: 新用戶會被詢問是否願意主動選擇接收個人化推薦。
exercises.upgrade: New users are asked whether they want to opt in to personalized recommendations.

options.explanation: are asked whether they want to clearly indicates explicit consent, which is the defining feature of opt in.
new users cannot renew something they have not already joined.
wrong type of activity.
recommendations are not necessarily a paid product.
opposite direction.
wrong sense of register.

falseSynonyms.zh: 追蹤 ≠ 所有 subscribe 在社交平台上 follow 和 subscribe 可能接近，但 follow 通常不建立付費訂閱或正式會員關係。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON You may follow a creator for updates, but subscribing can involve a formal or paid arrangement.

falseSynonyms.zh: 購買 ≠ 訂閱 buy 通常是一次性購買；subscription 通常持續一段時間。
註冊 ≠ 必然訂閱 register 只保證完成登記，不保證已購買或啟用訂閱。
報讀／登記加入 ≠ 一般媒體訂閱 enrol 主要用於 course / programme / scheme。
續訂 ≠ 首次訂閱 renew 表示延長已有 subscription。
取消訂閱 ≠ 訂閱 是相反方向的動作。
名詞 vs 動詞 - subscription = 訂閱 - subscribe = 訂閱
falseSynonyms.point: buy a subscription subscribe to a service

falseSynonyms.zh: 人 vs 動作 - subscriber = 訂戶 - subscribe = 訂閱
